title: Stellaris security QA field guide and evidence roadmap
content:
Purpose:
Quick field guide for the Stellaris POC security questionnaire and a pragmatic evidence roadmap we can execute in the next 6 weeks. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: highlight immediate artifacts we can assemble, outstanding technical gaps, and owner-level action items to get Stellaris to a state where they can close a vendor security review and proceed to Dedicated onboarding.

Context and scope:
- Customer: Stellaris Insurance (mid-market, regulated in NA and EU)
- Engagement: 6-week POC to validate Redwood Dedicated with KMS integration and audit evidence for core controls (access, encryption, change management, network isolation, logging/retention)
- This doc covers security questionnaire answers, evidence indexes, workshop notes from the 2026-01-20 architecture session, and a prioritized evidence collection plan.

High-level status snapshot (as of last_modified):
- Questionnaire initial pass: 70% completed by SE team (answers drafted)
- Evidence available: 40% of required artifacts (system diagrams, KMS config snapshots, RBAC maps)
- Gaps: automated audit logs export, recent patch evidence for image builds, signed SLA for Dedicated nodes
- Risk summary: Moderate - most gaps are collection/packaging rather than control failures

Key contacts:
- Aisha Patel (SE lead, owner) - aisha@redwood.ai
- Miguel Torres (SecEng, evidence lead) - miguel@redwood.ai
- Priya Shah (Customer Success) - priya@redwood.ai
- Stellaris security contact: Jenna Lowe, CISO (jenna.lowe@stellaris-ins.com)

Evidence inventory (index of artifacts we will deliver) - target format: PDF or signed export where possible
1) System component diagram (network zones, VPC endpoints, Dedicated cluster boundary, KMS boundary) - file: stellaris-system-diagram.pdf - owner: Aisha Patel - status: done (v1)
2) KMS integration snapshot (customer KMS key metadata + Redwood key-wrap config) - file: stellaris-kms-snapshot.txt - owner: Miguel Torres - status: partial (need rotation policy export)
3) RBAC and IAM mapping (roles, scopes, service accounts used during POC) - file: stellaris-rbac-map.xlsx - owner: Oliver Nguyen - status: draft
4) Logging & retention proof (sample CloudTrail/tenant-audit logs + retention policy) - file: stellaris-logs-sample.json - owner: Miguel Torres - status: partial (sample captured, retention policy doc pending)
5) Change management evidence (CI pipeline run artifacts, signed change requests for infra) - file: stellaris-ci-change-log.pdf - owner: Ethan Brooks - status: missing (action item)
6) Image and package patch statement (build image hash + SBOM) - file: stellaris-image-sbom.json - owner: Oliver Nguyen - status: missing (needs automation)
7) Vulnerability scan report (container/image scan for POC images) - file: stellaris-vuln-report.pdf - owner: Miguel Torres - status: scheduled
8) SLA & support attachments (Dedicated SLA excerpt, escalation contacts) - file: stellaris-dedicated-sla.pdf - owner: Aisha Patel - status: draft
9) Pen test / app-level assessment (summary of findings if performed) - file: stellaris-pen-test-summary.pdf - owner: Stellaris (customer) - status: optional

Questionnaire answer highlights (short-form) - representative Qs from Stellaris security packet:
- Q: Do you support customer-managed KMS for encryption of tenant keys?
  A: Yes. Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS where the customer can supply keys via AWS KMS / GCP KMS or HSM. We provide key wrap and do not store raw key material in our control plane. Evidence: KMS integration snapshot, KMS access policy export.
- Q: How do you isolate customer data in Dedicated?
  A: Network and compute isolation: Dedicated clusters run in customer VPCs (or VPC-peered projects) with strict routing, firewall rules, and node-level tenancy control. Artifacts: system component diagram, VPC peering config snippets.
- Q: Where are audit logs retained and how long?
  A: Audit logs are exported to a customer-managed logging GCS/S3 bucket; default retention policy is 365 days for POC but configurable. Evidence: logging export policy, sample logs.
- Q: How do you handle secrets and rotation?
  A: Secrets are stored in KMS-wrapped vaults; rotation is supported via scheduled key rotations. For Dedicated customers, we recommend a rotation cadence of 90 days. Evidence: rotation policy doc (pending) and KMS key metadata.

Workshop notes (2026-01-20 Architecture session) - raw scribbles and action items:
Attendees: Aisha (SE), Miguel (SecEng), Priya (CSM), Jenna (Stellaris CISO), Dan (Stellaris infra lead)
- Jenna stressed requirement for customer-managed KMS and proof of no plaintext key exfiltration. Action: Miguel to pull KMS access policy and export last 90 days of key usage logs (due 2026-01-25).
- Dan asked about network segmentation for data-at-rest vs control-plane telemetry. Action: Aisha to produce an annotated system diagram showing telemetry flow and control plane ingress points (due 2026-01-22).
- Priya asked for a one-page security summary for procurement team. Action: Aisha to draft a "security one-pager" targeting procurement (due 2026-01-28).
- Agreed to run an internal vulnerability scan of the POC images and share the results. Action: Oliver to schedule scan and upload report (due 2026-02-02).
- Noted: Stellaris wants signed evidence for patching of base images within last 30 days. Action: Ethan to capture the build pipeline run and attach the image hash + SBOM (due 2026-02-05).

Prioritized evidence collection plan (6-week cadence) - owners and milestones:
Week 0 (this week) - finalize questionnaire draft and send to Jenna for a preliminary read (owner: Aisha)
Week 1 - collect KMS policy exports, system diagram v1, RBAC draft (owners: Miguel, Aisha, Oliver)
Week 2 - run vulnerability scan, capture CI pipeline artifacts and image SBOM (owners: Oliver, Ethan)
Week 3 - assemble logging export proof, generate retention policy doc, compile signed SLA excerpt (owners: Miguel, Aisha)
Week 4 - quality-check package with SecEng, resolve any gaps flagged by Jenna, produce final evidence bundle v1 (owner: Miguel)
Week 5 - deliver evidence bundle to Stellaris and iterate on feedback (owner: Aisha/Priya)

Open risks and clarifying questions (to bring to next workshop):
- Can Stellaris provide an endpoint for a customer-managed logging bucket so we can validate export configs? (ask: Dan)
- Does Stellaris require SOC2 Type II artifacts specifically or will a SOC2 Type I + companion evidence suffice for this procurement? (ask: Jenna procurement team)
- Are there legal requirements for data residency beyond EU/US boundaries for the POC telemetry? If yes, we must package regional evidence separately.

Packaging guidance and signatures:
- Preferred artifact types: signed PDF exports, configuration screenshots with UTC timestamps, and immutable hash manifests (sha256) for container images.
- For any policy artifacts pulled from cloud consoles, include the export timestamp and the account identifier.
- We will provide an "EVIDENCE_MANIFEST.csv" at the root of the bundle that maps artifact file names to control IDs and owners.

Next meeting and deliverables:
- Next checkpoint: 2026-01-27 (30m) - review KMS export and system diagram. Expected deliverables before meeting: KMS export (Miguel), system diagram v1 (Aisha), RBAC map draft (Oliver).
- Final evidence handoff: target 2026-02-12 (deliver bundle and one-pager).

Notes to SEs (tips & snippets):
- When answering questionnaire Qs about encryption, use the phrase: "Customer-managed keys are supported; Redwood does not retain plaintext key material." That language resonates with enterprise infosec teams.
- Attach console screenshots with the "Export as JSON" button where possible (helps auditors).
- For time-sensitive evidence (e.g., patch dates), include CI run ids and build timestamps — auditors will ask for immutability.

Appendix A - quick checklist (tick when done):
- [ ] System diagram with annotated data flow
- [ ] KMS key metadata export + rotation policy
- [ ] RBAC mapping for services used in POC
- [ ] Logging export config + sample logs
- [ ] CI pipeline artifact showing image hash and SBOM
- [ ] Vulnerability scan report (container/image)
- [ ] Dedicated SLA excerpt with support contacts
- [ ] EVIDENCE_MANIFEST.csv linking artifacts to control IDs

Appendix B - sample questionnaire snippets (copyable):
- "Redwood Dedicated supports VPC-native deployment. Customer workloads run in a customer-controlled VPC with network ACLs and customer-managed routing. We can provide network config exports and peering manifests on request."
- "Audit logs are exported to a customer-specified storage endpoint; Redwood provides the export tooling and supports retention settings configurable by the customer."

Comments and freeform notes (working area):
- "If Stellaris asks for pen test, propose a scoped web/api test focusing on the inference endpoint only. Offer a timeboxed engagement and share a redacted summary rather than raw findings."
- "Consider offering a limited data residency demonstration: spin up a Dedicated node in eu-west-1 and run sample inference with telemetry disabled to show no egress."

End of document.
